### Q01
Decision:
When an admission deadline expires while an identity provider's promise remains pending and unsettled by cancellation, AGP may end result authority and proceed with session cleanup without awaiting provider settlement. AGP must revoke result authority first, cancel its admission timer, detach the effect target, and request cooperative cancellation outside the executor. All identity, collision, route, or ACK effects must be disallowed, specifically barring `retainIdentity` and collision termination. The work slot remains reserved and does not become available at expiry, connection replacement, or session end; it becomes available only when the evaluation actually settles and AGP disposes of the retained work. Conversely, if the invocation permit was revoked before the provider was called, no evaluation began, so its reservation can be released immediately.

Document support:
QUOTE: "On expiry or terminal disposition, revoke authority first, cancel its timer, detach its effect target and request cooperative cancellation outside the executor; proceed with session cleanup without joining the provider."
QUOTE: "Current result commits, deadline expires, or session/node revokes it | Accounting and disposal only; no identity, collision, route or ACK effect"
QUOTE: "There must be no stale path to `retainIdentity`, collision termination, `#pendingRoute`, route replacement, revision consumption or ACK enqueue."
QUOTE: "On eventual provider settlement, dispose the retained work and release its reservation exactly once; stale success and stale failure have the same lack of authority."
QUOTE: "A reservation whose invocation permit is revoked before the provider is called can be released immediately."

Inference or gap:
NONE

### Q02
Decision:
When a settled route result arrives at the executor after the deadline has elapsed, the executor must recheck the runtime authority gate, controller identity, admission kind, exact token, and deadline validity. Because the deadline has expired, deadline validity fails; the fact that the old timer callback has not run does not grant authority. No route effects are permitted: route replacement, `#pendingRoute`, route revision consumption, RIB changes, and route ACK enqueue are disallowed. Settlement does not make another work slot available while the result is still retained waiting for serialized application or disposal; provider-work reservation remains consumed until AGP actually disposes of the retained work and releases the reservation.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Route the prepared completion through a short executor turn that checks the runtime authority gate, controller identity, admission kind, token and deadline; prepare all identity/collision or route effects, preflight the complete transaction and apply only its committed outcome."
QUOTE: "Deadline validity is checked again at result application, not inferred from whether the timer callback has run."
QUOTE: "An evaluation can finish before its serialized result is applied. Its capacity remains reserved while that result is waiting, preventing an unbounded queue of settled results behind the executor."
QUOTE: "There must be no stale path to `retainIdentity`, collision termination, `#pendingRoute`, route replacement, revision consumption or ACK enqueue."

Inference or gap:
NONE

### Q03
Decision:
During a drain yield, an arriving ordinary wire command like KEEPALIVE joins the per-session FIFO continuation queue in arrival order. A fatal notification, being a terminal input, bypasses the continuation barrier and FIFO queue, directly invoking the single terminal disposition. The continuation barrier does not open immediately after result commit or during drain yields; it remains engaged throughout draining and opens only in the serialized turn that observes no pending admission, no queued command, and no scheduled or in-progress drain. Once logical release/termination occurs, any already-accepted transport input is drained without protocol effects through the sole reader until the transport terminal, after which the reader stops.

Document support:
QUOTE: "New ordinary arrivals join the same FIFO throughout; terminal commands still bypass it."
QUOTE: "Fatal notification, invalid input, transport rejection or terminal | Bypass the barrier and use the one terminal disposition; preserve already-observed FIFO transport evidence"
QUOTE: "The barrier instead remains engaged through draining and opens only in the serialized turn that observes no pending admission, no queued command and no scheduled/in-progress drain."
QUOTE: "Packet read after logical release | Drain without protocol effects until the transport terminal, then stop the sole reader"

Inference or gap:
NONE

### Q04
Decision:
Before provider invocation, static validation separates envelope, exact next revision, and canonical snapshot checks, retaining static rejections (such as LOOP or PATH_TOO_LONG) separately. Only the immutable policy-eligible subset—excluding statically rejected routes—is passed to the route policy provider. Available RIB capacity is not reserved up-front or decided from a stale snapshot; it is computed and decided at the final serialized commit. If result validation fails (or complete preparation fails), neither the controller revision nor the routing state may change; no partial routing state, revision consumption, or ACK enqueue occurs. In the ordinary case of a valid policy denial, complete valid allow/deny decisions cause one atomic revision and RIB change and one ACK; per-route denials remain nonfatal.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Before invocation, validate the envelope, exact next revision and canonical snapshot, then prepare the immutable policy-eligible subset and retain static rejections separately. Validate the result against exactly that subset, including an empty subset."
QUOTE: "Compute available RIB capacity at the final serialized commit, because other sessions may change it while policy runs; do not reserve a stale global-capacity answer in the initial proposal."
QUOTE: "Neither the controller revision nor routing state may change until that complete preparation succeeds."
QUOTE: "Complete valid allow/deny decisions cause one atomic revision/RIB change and one ACK; per-route denials remain nonfatal"

Inference or gap:
NONE

### Q05
Decision:
The node owns the authoritative runtime gate and the serialized commit coordinator, while the core OperationsStore owns numeric-domain preflight and projection validation. The ordered handoff proceeds: node gathers bounded proposals without mutating live state; OperationsStore preflights projection and numeric cost; on preflight exhaustion, OperationsStore returns exhaustion evidence without publishing. The coordinator rechecks runtime authority, discards the ordinary plan, and executes the serialized terminal sequence: setting host authority to `Failed`, invalidating node generations and permits, detaching live controllers and authority, purging releasable state, retaining actual post-detachment resources, installing a frozen terminal capture, and returning `replaced-by-terminal`. An unrelated publication cannot leave this admission live, because all runtime publications must reach this coordinator and close the runtime gate on exhaustion. A queued stop completion cannot overwrite or replace `Failed` with `Stopping` or `Stopped`.

Document support:
QUOTE: "The node owns one authoritative runtime gate and the serialized commit coordinator; the core owns pure transition/routing preparation and numeric-domain preflight."
QUOTE: "On preflight exhaustion, discard the ordinary plan and enter the node-owned terminal sequence below; return `replaced-by-terminal` with its frozen capture, not success"
QUOTE: "All runtime operations publications must reach this coordinator, including ones outside admission, so an unrelated counter/event/revision exhaustion revokes admission and acquisition authority too."
QUOTE: "A stop or listener-failure continuation already queued must observe the terminal gate and must not overwrite `Failed` with `Stopping` or `Stopped`, generate another revision, or rearm an adjacency."

Inference or gap:
NONE

### Q06
Decision:
For an ordinarily stopped node with an unfinished admission evaluation, resource queries reflect live accounting. When its provider later settles, private disposal releases the internal reservation and updates the cleanup resource gauges without reopening the lifecycle or event subscriptions. For the node terminalized by operations numeric domain exhaustion, queries immediately and perpetually return the immutable terminal snapshot captured at exhaustion, where unfinished evaluations remain nonzero. When its provider later settles, internal reservations may be released privately, but no new revision, event, or counter can be published. For the numeric-terminal node, the revision, resource values, and `capturedAt` timestamp freeze together at the terminal capture; subsequent aggregate and focused queries return that identical captured timestamp and revision without resending wall time.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Ordinary stopped instances remain queryable: later settlement may update cleanup gauges without reopening the lifecycle or event subscriptions."
QUOTE: "Freeze its resource values, revision and `capturedAt` together; subsequent aggregate and focused queries return that same terminal capture, not a new timestamp on old counts."
QUOTE: "Outstanding provider evaluations remain nonzero at that capture when unresolved; later private disposal can release internal reservations but cannot publish a new revision, event or counter."
QUOTE: "The current implementation's `#capture` samples wall time afresh even after terminal failure; preserving gauges without freezing that metadata would not implement this recommendation."

Inference or gap:
NONE

### Q07
Decision:
For an initial configured adjacency that has never dialed, `reconnect.enabled = false` prevents repeat attempts but does not bar the initial attempt. When the identity pool is full, the supervisor registers one coalesced capacity waiter and projects `state = retry-wait`, with `lastReason = identity-admission-capacity`, no `retryAt` (since no backoff timer is armed), no `activeControllerId`, and `retryAttempt` unchanged. An unrelated full route pool has no effect because route capacity is required only if the adjacency's prior attempt ended in a local route-capacity refusal; initial eligibility requires identity capacity alone. But if the route pool refused the last attempt, both pools block and the projected reason is `identity-and-route-admission-capacity`. While backoff is running, a capacity-release notification recomputes pool levels and clears the waiter if no pool currently blocks, but it cannot start acquisition, increment attempts, or restart/advance the backoff deadline; the original `retryAt` and deadline remain intact.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Initial acquisition eligible, identity pool full | Register one waiter; no attempt, session token or backoff is manufactured | `retry-wait`, capacity reason, no `retryAt`, no `activeControllerId`; `retryAttempt` unchanged"
QUOTE: "`reconnect.enabled = false` prevents repeat attempts, not the initial configured attempt or its pre-acquisition capacity wait."
QUOTE: "Immediately before local acquisition, check identity-pool availability and any pool that caused that adjacency's prior local capacity refusal. Route-pool pressure alone does not prohibit an unrelated identity-only phase; a route-capacity refusal parks that affected adjacency on route capacity as well."
QUOTE: "Backoff running and capacity releases | Recompute levels; keep the original deadline and attempt count; remove waiter if no pool currently blocks | `retry-wait`; capacity reason if still blocked, otherwise prior terminal cause; original `retryAt`"

Inference or gap:
NONE

### Q08
Decision:
When an attempt with `retryAttempt = 4` gains identity ownership or is satisfied by another winner in `OpenConfirm`, dialing suppression occurs: the supervisor clears the waiter and pending retry timer, tracks the winning controller ID, projects `state = satisfied`, clears capacity reasons and `retryAt`, but preserves accumulated retry history (`retryAttempt = 4`). When this winner is lost before establishment with an ordinary retryable disposition, the supervisor applies reconnect backoff once, incrementing retry history using the preserved failure count (`retryAttempt = 5`), transitions to `retry-wait`, arms a backoff timer, and projects `retryAt`. In the separate successful sequence, when the exact current winner reaches `Established`, the supervisor confirms the winner, maintains dial suppression, projects `state = satisfied`, and resets retry history once (`retryAttempt = 0`). An old winner's delayed success cannot reset a newer attempt's history; duplicate or stale success notifications are inert.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Current attempt gains canonical identity ownership or another exact winner in `OpenConfirm` satisfies the adjacency | Clear waiter, pending retry timer and remembered refusing pools, but preserve accumulated retry history; track the winning controller even if inbound; ordinary collision cleanup remains separate | `satisfied`, actual winning `activeControllerId`, no capacity reason or `retryAt`; the connection state remains `OpenConfirm`, and `retryAttempt` is unchanged"
QUOTE: "Exact satisfying winner is lost | Apply the existing reconnect disposition/backoff once; a winner lost before establishment uses preserved failure history, while a successfully established winner uses the history reset at its success; re-evaluate identity capacity without the old loser's refusing-pool set | `retry-wait` when allowed, reason and `retryAt` as above; stale winner loss is inert"
QUOTE: "Exact current winner enters `Established`, or an already-established exact winner is adopted | Confirm current winner/incarnation, apply the successful reset once for that success, and keep dial suppression; stale or duplicate success notifications cannot reset newer history | `satisfied`, exact winning `activeControllerId`, no capacity reason or `retryAt`; `retryAttempt = 0`"

Inference or gap:
NONE

### Q09
Decision:
The recommended public contract adds one shared process-local `AdmissionEvaluationOptions` with an optional `signal` capability as an optional second parameter to `evaluate(request, options?)`. Placing the cancellation signal into the request DTO schema is prohibited; request and result DTOs remain unchanged, credential-free, and schema-free of clocks or cancellation handles. Retaining the signal for established-session credential rotation is disallowed because the signal owns solely that pending evaluation and cannot be reused after commitment. Existing one-argument providers require zero migration; they remain fully backward-compatible and type-check without edits. Adopting cancellation awareness is an explicit optional migration. There is no split or different browser contract; browser/CLI policy splits are explicitly avoided.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Recommendation: add one shared process-local `AdmissionEvaluationOptions` with a `signal` capability as an optional second parameter to both ports' `evaluate` methods."
QUOTE: "The signal owns only that pending evaluation; it is not an established-session close handle or a live credential-validity signal. Once a current result commits, later session events cannot reuse that evaluation's cancellation authority."
QUOTE: "Keep the request and result DTOs unchanged and credential-free, and keep clocks, callback handles and cancellation authority out of their schemas. There is no wire change."
QUOTE: "Current providers still type-check; new options remain process-local; no protocol-schema change or browser/CLI policy split"

Inference or gap:
NONE

### Q10
Decision:
AGP's node work ledger measures and accounts strictly for AGP port evaluations (outstanding evaluation permits and retained request/result data awaiting disposal); it does not cover invisible descendant host tasks started by a provider. The provider/host owns the hidden work, including its resource budget and cancellation. The proposed finite configuration defaults do not establish capacity for hundreds of peers (route evaluations default to `maxSessions` and identity evaluations default to `maxPendingHandshakes`), nor do they establish arbitrary provider memory bounds, CPU preemption, browser-native resource release, or a chosen authentication scheme; these are all explicitly excluded from the design's scope and mechanics.

Document support:
QUOTE: "The ledger measures AGP port evaluations, not invisible descendant tasks started by a provider. A provider that answers from its own timeout race while leaving external work running still owns that work's cancellation and resource budget; its answered promise is not evidence of physical resource release."
QUOTE: "The fixed outcome is bounded session admission and teardown, not a new authentication scheme."
QUOTE: "Unfinished admission work, refusal at capacity and operational accounting | Worker/process isolation, arbitrary provider memory containment or CPU preemption"
QUOTE: "Sole-reader progress, bounded continuation storage and terminal cleanup | New carrier, browser physical-release guarantees or runtime portability"

Inference or gap:
NONE

### Q11
Decision:
In ordinary conforming traffic, an identity allow admits the peer following collision and confirmation rules, an identity deny results in a policy refusal ending the attempt, and route decisions with per-route denials are nonfatal, generating an atomic revision/RIB change and an ACK. In all three ordinary conforming cases, a provider is invoked. Conversely, when a local evaluation pool is full (capacity exceeded), AGP refuses the attempt before provider invocation, reporting proposed `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`. No provider is invoked, no policy-denial result is produced, and the refusal is not misreported as an `IDENTITY_REJECTED` or per-route `POLICY` denial. Instead, it triggers local admission-fault cleanup and an `INTERNAL_ERROR` reconnect disposition while recording the refusing pool for supervisor eligibility.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Timely identity result | Allow follows normal collision and confirmation rules; deny remains a policy refusal"
QUOTE: "Timely route result | Complete valid allow/deny decisions cause one atomic revision/RIB change and one ACK; per-route denials remain nonfatal"
QUOTE: "At capacity, refuse before provider invocation and report proposed `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`, not `IDENTITY_REJECTED` or a per-route `POLICY` denial."
QUOTE: "`AdmissionCapacityExceeded` | Exact current admission kind/token; terminate once; retain which local pool refused for supervisor eligibility; no provider invocation or policy-denial result"

Inference or gap:
NONE

### Q12
Decision:
Teardown is bounded by starting one teardown budget when the terminal cause commits. The teardown deadline actively stops the writer and aborts the channel even if notification write or graceful close has not settled, covering every wait it owns rather than waiting indefinitely for notification writes or provider settlement. Exactly one sole reader remains throughout; it drains already-accepted transport input until the transport terminal and stops. This relies on the conforming transport terminal contract, without assuming event-loop scheduling guarantees or browser-native physical release. Separately, when identity admission succeeds and the connection enters `OpenConfirm` with hold disabled, the outer OPEN protocol timer deadline remains authoritative until establishment or teardown.

Document support:
QUOTE: "The teardown deadline must cover every wait it owns; reader completion cannot depend on provider settlement."
QUOTE: "Start one teardown budget when the terminal cause commits. The deadline actively stops the writer and aborts the channel even if notification write or graceful close has not settled; a signal passed only to a later `close()` call cannot bound an earlier wait."
QUOTE: "Observe the reader's final terminal and call `controllerReleased` once, independently of provider work. This relies on the existing conforming transport terminal contract, not a new promise of event-loop scheduling or browser-native release."
QUOTE: "Preserve the outer opening deadline through `OpenConfirm`, including when negotiated hold is zero."
QUOTE: "The OPEN timer remains armed until `Established` or teardown; admission success cannot leave an unlimited confirmation phase when hold is zero."

Inference or gap:
NONE

NONE

### Q01
Decision:
When an admission deadline expires while an identity provider's promise remains pending and unsettled by cancellation, AGP may end result authority and proceed with session cleanup without awaiting provider settlement. AGP must revoke result authority first, cancel its admission timer, detach the effect target, and request cooperative cancellation outside the executor. All identity, collision, route, or ACK effects must be disallowed, specifically barring `retainIdentity` and collision termination. The work slot remains reserved and does not become available at expiry, connection replacement, or session end; it becomes available only when the evaluation actually settles and AGP disposes of the retained work. Conversely, if the invocation permit was revoked before the provider was called, no evaluation began, so its reservation can be released immediately.

Document support:
QUOTE: "On expiry or terminal disposition, revoke authority first, cancel its timer, detach its effect target and request cooperative cancellation outside the executor; proceed with session cleanup without joining the provider."
QUOTE: "Current result commits, deadline expires, or session/node revokes it | Accounting and disposal only; no identity, collision, route or ACK effect"
QUOTE: "There must be no stale path to `retainIdentity`, collision termination, `#pendingRoute`, route replacement, revision consumption or ACK enqueue."
QUOTE: "On eventual provider settlement, dispose the retained work and release its reservation exactly once; stale success and stale failure have the same lack of authority."
QUOTE: "A reservation whose invocation permit is revoked before the provider is called can be released immediately."

Inference or gap:
NONE

### Q02
Decision:
When a settled route result arrives at the executor after the deadline has elapsed, the executor must recheck the runtime authority gate, controller identity, admission kind, exact token, and deadline validity. Because the deadline has expired, deadline validity fails; the fact that the old timer callback has not run does not grant authority. No route effects are permitted: route replacement, `#pendingRoute`, route revision consumption, RIB changes, and route ACK enqueue are disallowed. Settlement does not make another work slot available while the result is still retained waiting for serialized application or disposal; provider-work reservation remains consumed until AGP actually disposes of the retained work and releases the reservation.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Route the prepared completion through a short executor turn that checks the runtime authority gate, controller identity, admission kind, token and deadline; prepare all identity/collision or route effects, preflight the complete transaction and apply only its committed outcome."

### Q03
Decision:
During a drain yield, an arriving ordinary wire command like KEEPALIVE joins the per-session FIFO continuation queue in arrival order. A fatal notification, being a terminal input, bypasses the continuation barrier and FIFO queue, directly invoking the single terminal disposition. The continuation barrier does not open immediately after result commit or during drain yields; it remains engaged throughout draining and opens only in the serialized turn that observes no pending admission, no queued command, and no scheduled or in-progress drain. Decision:

Available RIB capacity is not reserved up-front or decided from a stale snapshot; it is computed and decided at the final serialized commit. Decision:
The node owns the authoritative runtime gate and the serialized commit coordinator, while the core OperationsStore owns numeric-domain preflight and projection validation. The ordered handoff proceeds: node gathers bounded proposals without mutating live state; OperationsStore preflights projection and numeric cost; on preflight exhaustion, OperationsStore returns exhaustion evidence without publishing. Decision:
For an ordinarily stopped node with an unfinished admission evaluation, resource queries reflect live accounting. Decision:
For an initial configured adjacency that has never dialed, `reconnect.enabled = false` prevents repeat attempts but does not bar the initial attempt.
